evidence.title: MIT ES.1803 topic notes, Fourier approximation
evidence.finding: Fourier expansions use harmonics and require a convergence interpretation. At a jump, ordinary partial sums converge to the midpoint under standard regularity hypotheses.

Changing the value at one jump of a square wave does not change any Fourier coefficient. Under the standard convergence theorem the series converges there to the midpoint, not an arbitrary assigned value.
This hold does not dispute Fourier representation in L2 or for standard piecewise-smooth waveforms with appropriate convergence meaning.
